Decision summary. The respondent is an organisation that held customer records in an online system. An unauthorised party obtained access to that system through credentials that had not been rotated.

Findings. The Commission found that the respondent had not put in place reasonable security arrangements to protect the personal data in its possession. Access controls were weak and no monitoring was in place.

Directions. The Commission directed the respondent to pay a financial penalty of S$12,000 within thirty days and to review its access management procedures and report back on the changes made.

Reasons. In deciding the amount, the Commission considered the number of individuals affected, the sensitivity of the data, the prompt notification of the incident, and the cooperation shown during the investigation.
